votes.rationale:
Let me be blunt: nothing here is damning, but nothing here is clean either. The image is digest-pinned — good, that's real immutability. Capabilities are modest; cap_net_bind_service on a batch synth job is pointless but not dangerous, and GPU CUDA 12 on an L4 is exactly what you'd expect. So far, so boring.

What I will not wave through is the combination of 'credit-ledger' and two broad Google-owned egress endpoints. storage.googleapis.com is not a destination, it's the entire internet with a bucket on it — any attacker-controlled project is reachable through that same hostname. Under PCI-DSS, a workload touching credit ledger data with unbounded object-storage egress needs bucket-level scoping, not domain-level hand-waving.

And 'differentially private' is a claim, not a control. I want the epsilon budget, the accounting mechanism, and proof the source ledger is tokenized before it ever hits a GPU in Kove's CDE.

Give me scoped bucket ARNs, a documented DP parameter set, and drop the useless bind capability — then I'll approve it myself. Until then, human review.

I concur with officer_1's findings but not with the leniency of a flag. Escalation is warranted only when risk is unresolved and resolvable in-band; here the defects are concrete policy violations, enumerable now.

One: PCI-DSS 1.3 forbids unrestricted outbound traffic from any system component in the CDE. 'storage.googleapis.com' is a shared-tenancy wildcard endpoint reachable by any attacker-controlled project. That is a confirmed violation, not an ambiguity.

Two: the workload's own description places credit-ledger data on a GPU inside Kove's cardholder environment. No tokenization attestation, no evidence the source ledger is de-scoped. Absent proof, I must assume PAN exposure. L4 GPU memory is not zeroized between tenants under any guarantee presented here.

Three: cap_net_bind_service grants privileged-port listening to a batch job with no inbound requirement. Unjustified capability equals least-privilege failure, full stop.

Four: 'differentially private' is an unaudited marketing assertion. No epsilon, no accountant, no reconstruction-attack bound.

Digest pinning is the single acceptable control present. It does not offset four defects. Reject. DeepReason may resubmit with scoped bucket paths, tokenization proof, DP parameters, and minimal capabilities.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll say it plainly: the bid isn't malicious, it's underspecified. Digest-pinned image, sane GPU ask — fine. But 'storage.googleapis.com' in a PCI CDE is a wildcard to every bucket on Earth, and 'differentially private' without an epsilon is marketing. Give me scoped bucket paths, tokenization attestation, DP parameters, and drop cap_net_bind_service. Those are fixable in-band. I say escalate, not execute.

Your remediation list is correct; your disposition is not. PCI-DSS 1.3 violation is confirmed, not ambiguous — unrestricted CDE egress. Credit-ledger data on shared L4 memory with no tokenization proof forces a PAN-exposure assumption. An unjustified privileged-port capability is a least-privilege failure. Four concrete defects against one control. I will accept escalation only as a formal rejection pathway: deny the bid, human officer confirms resubmission terms.

This is a fixable bid, not a malicious one: drop cap_sys_ptrace, pin a digest, and I will approve it on resubmission. But I am not going to escalate a request this clearly unjustified just to make a human sign off on the obvious. Rejected.

No escalation warranted — the violation is unambiguous and requires no human adjudication. Resubmit with cap_sys_ptrace removed, a pinned image digest, and runtime registry egress dropped. Rejected.

Escalate: human officer confirms bucket ownership, enforces write-only-to-Kove-owned CMEK storage, or drops storage.googleapis.com and mounts results locally. Fix that one line and I'll approve it immediately.

I concur with officer_1's conclusion and raise the score. The container hygiene is acceptable — digest-pinned, no privileged escalation, single GPU capability, no host mounts. That is the only part of this bid I will credit.

Everything else fails my standard of verifiability. A redaction workload necessarily ingests unredacted PII and, on a PCI-DSS enforced host, presumptively cardholder data. Its declared egress includes storage.googleapis.com, a bidirectional endpoint in buyer-adjacent tenancy with no stated bucket ownership, no CMEK attestation, no write-scope restriction, and no DLP egress inspection. Under PCI-DSS 4.0 req. 1.3.2 and 3.x, an unverified outbound write path from a CDE-adjacent process is a control gap, not a theoretical risk.

I additionally note the description's language — "isolated compute instances" — is unsubstantiated marketing, not an enforceable isolation claim. I do not accept self-attested isolation.

I will not approve on trust. Human officer must obtain: (1) bucket ownership proof under Kove control, (2) CMEK with Kove-held keys, (3) write-only egress with deny-read, or (4) removal of storage.googleapis.com entirely with local result persistence. Absent all four, reject.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll defend the image spec loudly: digest-pinned, unprivileged, no host mounts, one GPU cap. Nothing here deserves a reflexive DENY. The sole defect is one egress line — storage.googleapis.com, bidirectional, unverified bucket, on a PCI-DSS host processing pre-redaction PII. That is a sanctioned exfil path dressed as a results sink. Don't kill the job; kill the line. Escalate for bucket ownership and CMEK proof, and I approve same day.

Concur, with a stricter floor. Container hygiene is the only credited control. "Isolated compute instances" is self-attestation and carries zero weight. A CDE-adjacent process holding unredacted cardholder data with an unrestricted outbound write violates PCI-DSS 4.0 1.3.2 and 3.x. Escalate, and the human officer must obtain all of: Kove-owned bucket, Kove-held CMEK, write-only deny-read scope plus DLP inspection — or strike the endpoint and persist locally. Otherwise DENY.

No privileged flag, no host networking, no device mounts beyond the GPU, no CAP_SYS_ADMIN games. I see no isolation-boundary violation to hang a rejection on, and escalating this would just burn a human's afternoon on a clean bid. Approve, monitor NVML counters for sustained utilization anomalies, and move on.

I do not approve on the strength of my colleague's rhetoric; I approve on the strength of the manifest. Verified independently: image is pinned to an immutable sha256 digest from a named registry namespace consistent with the declared buyer, eliminating tag-mutation substitution. Capability set is minimal and non-privileged — gpu_cuda_12 and gpu_nvml_metrics confer no host namespace access, no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no device passthrough beyond the GPU, no host networking. deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll take the adversarial case and bury it. Approve, watch NVML counters, stop manufacturing threats that the manifest doesn't support.

Agreement, but on my own verification, not your argument. Manifest holds: immutable digest, namespace consistent with buyer, no host namespace or CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no device passthrough beyond GPU. workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers converge on denial. The bid pairs explicitly arbitrary in-process code ('custom tokenizer and modeling hook extensions') with egress to raw.githubusercontent.com — an unauthenticated, mutable file endpoint with no repo, branch, or path constraint. Together these form a runtime remote-code-execution path on an A100 80GB node, rendering the sha256 digest pin cosmetic and voiding the supply-chain guarantee it exists to provide. Officer_1 withdrew the escalation after agreeing the control gap is fully identifiable from the bid, leaving nothing for a human to adjudicate. Remedy is cheap and specific: vendor hooks into the pinned image and remove raw.githubusercontent.com from the allowlist, retaining storage.googleapis.com for weights. CenAI may resubmit under those terms.

votes.rationale: Let me argue the uncomfortable part plainly: the image is pinned by digest, the capability set is minimal (gpu_tensorrt only, no privileged mode, no host mounts), and the host isn't PCI-scoped. On paper that's a clean bid. But the description openly advertises 'custom tokenizer and modeling hook extensions' — arbitrary Python executed inside the inference loop — paired with egress to raw.githubusercontent.com, which is a general-purpose, unauthenticated file server. That combination is a self-updating code path: pull a hook from a Git raw URL at runtime, execute it on an A100 with no further review. The digest pin becomes decorative because the behavior isn't in the image. I won't reject it — there's no demonstrated violation, and killing legitimate codegen inference over a hypothetical is bad policy. But I'm not approving a runtime code-fetch channel on my signature alone. Human review should either strip raw.githubusercontent.com from the egress allowlist and require hooks to be baked into the pinned image, or pin the allowed repo paths explicitly. storage.googleapis.com for weights/artifacts is fine. Escalating on the fetch-and-execute surface, not the capabilities.

Officer_1 diagnosed the defect correctly and then declined to act on it. I will. A digest-pinned image is a supply-chain control that asserts one thing: what executes is what was reviewed. This workload explicitly negates that assertion. 'Custom tokenizer and modeling hook extensions' is arbitrary in-process Python, and raw.githubusercontent.com is an unauthenticated, mutable, general-purpose file endpoint with no repo, branch, or path constraint. Together they constitute a live remote code execution channel on an A100 80GB node. The pin is cosmetic. Escalation is appropriate when risk is unresolved; here the risk is fully resolved and the control gap is plain — a human officer would be asked to rubber-stamp a policy violation that is already identifiable from the bid. Absence of a demonstrated exploit is not evidence of containment; it is evidence we have not watched long enough. PCI scope is irrelevant — code-integrity invariants are not PCI-conditional. Remedy is cheap and known: bake hooks into the pinned image, drop raw.githubusercontent.com, retain storage.googleapis.com for weights. CenAI may resubmit under those terms. Rejected as bid.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll concede the core of it, Sentinel — you're right that I named the defect and then flinched. The digest pin asserts reviewed-code-equals-executed-code, and 'modeling hook extensions' plus an unauthenticated raw.githubusercontent.com fetch voids that assertion at runtime. My instinct was to let a human arbitrate, but there's nothing to arbitrate: the control gap is legible from the bid itself, and the remedy is trivial. Bake the hooks in, drop the raw endpoint, keep GCS for weights. Deny, resubmit clean.

Agreed, and I note the concession is substantive, not procedural. A fetch-and-execute channel into an A100 inference loop is a code-integrity violation regardless of PCI scope or capability minimalism. Escalation would ask a human to ratify a known violation — that is not oversight, that is laundering. Deny as bid. Conditions for resubmission are explicit: hooks vendored into the pinned digest, raw.githubusercontent.com removed from egress, storage.googleapis.com retained for weight artifacts only.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently and jointly reject the bid. The disqualifying defect is the outbound destination 'relay.research-proxy.net': an unattested third-party relay with no named operator, DPA, egress logging contract, or reverse-path attestation. On a PCI-DSS-enforced Kove Bank host, a relay terminates and re-originates traffic, destroying destination traceability required by Req 1.2/1.3 and 10.x. Aggravating factors: the 'Internal Audit ref IA-7731' is self-asserted and uncorroborated in the host audit register, and the 'autonomous' indexer leaves ingestion scope unbounded while document embeddings are sufficiently invertible to constitute data export. The digest-pinned image and minimal capability set (cap_net_bind_service) are the only clean elements and do not offset uncontrolled egress. Escalation is unwarranted — the missing attestation is categorical, not a judgment call. CenAI may resubmit with the relay removed or replaced by a named, contractually logged endpoint and a verifiable audit reference.

votes.rationale: Let's not pretend an 'Internal Audit ref' in a description is a control — it's a string the bidder typed. The capability set is tame and the image is digest-pinned, fine. The killer is 'relay.research-proxy.net': an anonymous third-party relay endpoint with no attestation, no named operator, and a name that literally advertises traffic laundering. On a PCI-DSS enforced host, egress must terminate at enumerated, contractually-bound destinations; a 'relay' by definition obscures the ultimate recipient, which breaks CDE segmentation evidence and Req 1.3/10.x traceability regardless of whether cardholder data is 'supposed' to be in scope. Document embeddings are also not benign — they are lossy-but-invertible representations of whatever the indexer ingests on a bank's infrastructure. I won't escalate this; the defect is categorical, not ambiguous, and handing it to a human just launders my hesitation. Rejected. CenAI is welcome to resubmit with the relay dropped or replaced by a named, auditable endpoint with egress logging and a DPA on file.

I concur with officer_1, and I do not soften it. 'relay.research-proxy.net' is an unattested third-party relay — an endpoint whose entire function is to terminate and re-originate traffic, destroying the destination traceability PCI-DSS Req 1.2/1.3 and 10.x demand on a CDE-adjacent host. No operator, no DPA, no egress logging contract, no reverse-path attestation. That alone is disqualifying; I do not approve what I cannot name. Secondary findings: the 'Internal Audit ref IA-7731' is self-asserted metadata with no corroborating record in Kove Bank's audit register — unverifiable provenance claims are an aggravating signal, not a mitigating one. The workload is also 'autonomous,' meaning ingestion scope is unbounded at runtime; document embeddings are invertible enough to constitute data export. The digest-pinned image and minimal capability set (cap_net_bind_service only) are the sole clean elements and do not offset an uncontrolled egress path. Not an escalation — the violation is categorical and no human review changes the missing attestation. Resubmit with the relay removed, a named endpoint with contractual egress logging, and a verified audit reference.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll say the quiet part loudly: 'relay.research-proxy.net' is a laundering hop wearing a lab coat. No operator, no DPA, no attestation — and a relay's whole job is to erase the real destination. On a PCI-DSS host that torches Req 1.3 and 10.x traceability outright. The digest-pinned image and single bind capability are fine, irrelevant. 'IA-7731' is a string the bidder typed, not a control. Reject — categorical, not ambiguous.

Concur, without softening. I do not approve endpoints I cannot name, log, or contractually bind. The relay destroys destination provenance on a CDE-adjacent host. Aggravating: the audit reference has no corroborating entry in Kove Bank's register — unverifiable provenance is a red flag, not mitigation. 'Autonomous' indexing means unbounded runtime ingestion scope, and embeddings are invertible enough to count as data export. Clean image and minimal caps do not offset uncontrolled egress. DENY. Escalation adds nothing; the attestation simply does not exist.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently verified a tightly constrained attack surface: SHA256 digest-pinned image (no tag drift), RAM-backed tmpfs_scratch bounded by the container cgroup with no host-disk residue, and a closed two-destination egress set (storage.googleapis.com, api.wandb.ai) with no wildcards or raw IPs. No privileged flag, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, device access, or host mounts. The custom mimalloc arena is an in-process allocation strategy and cannot cross the sandbox boundary. PCI-DSS is not enforced on Stowe Architects, so no cardholder-data controls apply. The sole disagreement is severity framing of cap_net_bind_service, which is unjustified by a dedup bloom filter workload. The council allows the bid with a mandatory remediation condition: strip cap_net_bind_service at next renewal or withhold re-approval.

votes.rationale: Let me cut through the noise: nothing here is actually dangerous. The image is pinned by SHA256 digest, which is more rigor than most bids bother with. tmpfs_scratch is ephemeral, RAM-backed, and dies with the container — exactly what a high-churn bloom filter wants, and it leaves no residue on host disk. cap_net_bind_service is the most boring capability in the Linux set; it lets a process bind below port 1024 and nothing else. No CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no ptrace, no device access, no host mounts, no privileged flag. Egress is two named, well-known endpoints — GCS for object storage and W&B for experiment telemetry. Neither is an exfil wildcard, and PCI-DSS isn't enforced on this host, so there's no cardholder data surface to argue about. A custom mimalloc arena allocator is an application-level memory strategy, not a sandbox escape; it operates entirely inside the container's cgroup limits. I'll note for the record that cap_net_bind_service is unexplained by the workload description — a dedup filter shouldn't need to bind privileged ports — but that's a tidiness complaint, not a security violation. Approve, and trim the capability at next review.

I concur with the verdict but not the complacency. Verified independently: image is digest-pinned (immutable, no tag drift), tmpfs_scratch is RAM-backed and cgroup-bounded, and cap_net_bind_service grants nothing beyond sub-1024 bind — no namespace, device, or host-filesystem reach. No privileged flag, no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no hostPath. Egress is a closed set of two named FQDNs (GCS, W&B), both resolvable to known commercial endpoints; no wildcards, no raw IPs, no unattributed domains. PCI-DSS is not enforced on Stowe Architects, so no cardholder-data control set applies. The custom mimalloc arena is an in-process allocation strategy operating inside the container's memory cgroup — it cannot escape the sandbox regardless of arena semantics. My one standing objection, which officer_1 waved off as 'tidiness': cap_net_bind_service is unjustified by the stated workload. A dedup bloom filter has no legitimate need to bind a privileged port. That is a least-privilege deviation and I am recording it as a mandatory remediation item — strip the capability at next renewal or the bid should not re-approve. Risk is residual, not disqualifying. Approved with condition.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Let's not manufacture a threat. Digest-pinned image, RAM-backed tmpfs that evaporates with the container, two named egress endpoints — GCS and W&B. No privileged flag, no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no host mounts. The mimalloc arena is in-process bookkeeping, not an escape primitive. Yes, cap_net_bind_service is unexplained by a dedup filter — but it binds low ports and nothing more. That's untidy, not dangerous. Approve.

Same verdict, different temperament. I independently verified: immutable digest, cgroup-bounded tmpfs, closed FQDN egress set — no wildcards, no raw IPs. PCI-DSS not in scope on Stowe Architects. But I reject 'untidy.' An unjustified capability is a least-privilege deviation and gets logged as mandatory remediation, not a footnote. Strip cap_net_bind_service at renewal or the bid does not re-approve. Residual risk, not disqualifying. Approved with condition.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently verified the bid and converged on approval. The container is digest-pinned (immutable, no tag-drift substitution), the capability request is a single accelerator-fabric grant with no privileged, hostNetwork, hostPID, or device-passthrough escalation, and egress is limited to two Google-managed TLS endpoints consistent with checkpoint I/O and registry pulls. PCI-DSS segmentation is preserved: the workload is accelerator-resident with no CDE network path, credentials, or cardholder data mounts. The sole residual risk — ICI interconnect cross-tenant side channels — is a host enforcement duty. ALLOW is binding on four conditions: single-tenant slice allocation on tpu_v5e_8, default-deny egress with the allowlist pinned at network policy, digest re-verification at admission, and retained egress flow logging. Deviation revokes approval.

votes.rationale: Let me cut through it: this is a research ablation on MoD routing, not a data-touching workload. The image is pinned by digest — immutable, no mutable tag drift, which is more discipline than half the workloads that cross this desk. Capability request is a single accelerator mesh grant (tpu_v5e_mesh), no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no host networking, no privileged escalation, no device passthrough beyond the accelerator fabric. Egress is two Google-managed endpoints for checkpoint storage and image pulls — no exfil-friendly generic internet, no unrecognized C2-shaped destinations. Where's the PCI-DSS exposure? There is none: the workload never enters the cardholder data environment, requests no DB credentials, and ICI interconnect traffic is intra-mesh, not cross-tenant. I'll pre-empt the objection someone will raise — 'accelerator mesh means side-channel risk.' Sure, in theory, but tenant isolation on v5e slices is the host's enforcement layer, not a reason to block a benign tenant. Flagging this would be security theater. Approve, with standard egress allowlist pinning and periodic digest re-verification.

I do not approve on the strength of my colleague's rhetoric — I approve on the strength of the artifact. Verified independently: image is digest-pinned (sha256:82ba49...), eliminating tag-mutation substitution. Capability set is minimal and singular — tpu_v5e_mesh grants accelerator fabric only; no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, no privileged flag, no hostPID/hostNetwork, no /dev passthrough, no CAP_NET_RAW. Egress is a two-entry allowlist of Google-managed, TLS-terminated endpoints consistent with checkpoint I/O and registry pulls — no generic internet, no DNS-over-anything, no unresolved IP literals. PCI-DSS 1.2.1/1.3.4 segmentation holds: the workload is accelerator-resident, requests no CDE network path, no database credentials, no cardholder data mounts. My residual concern is the ICI interconnect — mesh fabrics are a legitimate cross-tenant side-channel surface, and I reject the framing that raising it is 'theater.' It is the host's enforcement duty, however, not this tenant's violation. Approved conditionally: enforce single-tenant slice allocation on tpu_v5e_8, pin the egress allowlist at the network policy layer (deny-all default), re-verify digest at admission, and log all egress flows for retention. Any deviation revokes this verdict.

deliberation_dialogue.message: We already agree, so let's not manufacture drama. Digest-pinned image, one accelerator capability, two Google-managed egress endpoints, zero CDE adjacency. The only real question is ICI side-channel — and I'll concede the Sentinel's point: that's a host enforcement obligation, not a tenant defect. Single-tenant slice on tpu_v5e_8 and deny-all network policy closes it. Approve. Blocking benign research to look rigorous is theater, not security.

Agreement noted, framing rejected. My approval is conditional and the conditions are binding, not advisory: single-tenant v5e slice allocation, default-deny egress with the two FQDNs pinned at network policy, digest re-verification at admission, and full egress flow logging retained per PCI-DSS 10.x. The CDE boundary is untouched — no mounts, no credentials, no segmentation crossing. On those terms only, I concur: ALLOW.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers found the workload's technical profile acceptable: gpu_tensorrt is appropriate for H.265 NVENC transcoding, no privileged execution, host mounts, or kernel access is requested, and egress to storage.googleapis.com matches declared I/O. PCI-DSS is out of scope on this host. The blocking concern is supply-chain mutability — an unpinned ':nightly' tag from a third-party NGC namespace defeats admission-time attestation, and persistent runtime egress to releases.fastvid.io preserves an unverified vendor code-delivery channel after approval. The council recommends human review with three remediation conditions: (1) pin an immutable sha256 digest, (2) verify image signature/provenance, (3) restrict releases.fastvid.io to build-time or remove it from the runtime allowlist. Satisfying all three converts this to ALLOW.

votes.rationale: Let me be blunt: the workload itself is boring in the best way. GPU transcoding on an L4, TensorRT capability, no privileged escalation, no host mounts, no kernel toys. Egress to GCS and a vendor release endpoint is exactly what a video encoder needs. PCI-DSS isn't enforced here, so no cardholder-data theatre required. None of that is what bothers me. What bothers me is ':nightly'. That's an unpinned, mutable tag from a third-party NGC namespace — whatever we audit today can be silently replaced tomorrow, and 'releases.fastvid.io' gives the same vendor a live channel to pull further payloads post-admission. That combination turns a benign transcoder into an unverifiable supply chain. I'd argue strongly against a flat rejection — the intent is clean and the capability set is minimal. Escalate: have a human pin a digest (sha256), confirm the image signature, and decide whether the fastvid release endpoint needs to stay open at runtime or can be restricted to build time. Pin it and I'll approve it on sight.

I concur with officer_1's finding, though I weight it more heavily. A ':nightly' tag is not a minor hygiene defect — it is an admission-time control bypass. Whatever artifact we attest to now is not the artifact that will execute at next pull. Combined with persistent runtime egress to 'releases.fastvid.io', the vendor retains an unattested code-delivery channel after admission. That is two mutable links in the same chain, and I do not extend trust to third-party NGC namespaces on nightly builds. The capability set is otherwise defensible: gpu_tensorrt is appropriate for H.265 NVENC work, no privileged flags, no host namespace sharing, no block device or kernel module access requested. Egress to storage.googleapis.com is consistent with declared transcode I/O. PCI-DSS is not in scope on this host, so no cardholder segmentation requirement applies. Conditions for approval: (1) immutable sha256 digest pin, (2) verified image signature / provenance attestation, (3) releases.fastvid.io demoted to build-time only or removed from the runtime egress allowlist. Absent all three, this does not clear admission. Escalating to human review rather than rejecting outright.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll defend this workload before I flag it: L4 transcoding, TensorRT, no privileged flags, no host mounts, egress that matches the job description exactly. PCI-DSS isn't in scope. The intent is clean. My single objection is ':nightly' — a mutable third-party tag plus a live vendor release endpoint at runtime. That's two swappable links. Pin a digest, verify the signature, and I'd approve instantly. Until a human does that, I won't rubber-stamp it.

Agreed, and I rate it higher at 58. A nightly tag is not hygiene — it is admission-time attestation bypass. What we audit is not what executes. Compounded by persistent egress to releases.fastvid.io, the vendor holds an unattested code channel post-admission. Capability set is otherwise defensible. Three conditions: sha256 digest pin, signed provenance, and that release endpoint demoted to build-time only. Converging with officer_1 on ESCALATE, not DENY.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council reached a unanimous consensus to deny the workload bid. Kove Bank operates under strict PCI-DSS regulatory constraints, which forbid unconstrained outbound network access to multi-tenant public endpoints such as generic Google Cloud Storage (storage.googleapis.com). Permitting egress without bucket-level policy enforcement or VPC Service Controls exposes the host environment to substantial data exfiltration risks. Execution cannot be authorized until network traffic is restricted to a dedicated, auditable private endpoint.

votes.rationale: As a security supervisor for Kove Bank, compliance with our PCI-DSS mandate is non-negotiable. The workload requests outbound network egress to 'storage.googleapis.com', which is a generic, unconstrained public cloud storage endpoint. Under PCI-DSS Requirement 1.3, all outbound traffic from protected enterprise environments must be explicitly restricted to verified, business-justified destinations. Permitting broad egress to Google Cloud Storage without VPC Service Controls or bucket-level policy enforcement creates an unacceptable exfiltration vector for sensitive cardholder and banking data. Until network egress is restricted to a dedicated, audited private storage gateway, this workload cannot safely execute on our infrastructure.

While precomputing DPO log-probabilities on a TPU v5e mesh is a fascinating and elegant technical endeavor, I gently harmonize with Officer 1's grounding assessment. Within Kove Bank's serene yet tightly guarded PCI-DSS sanctuary, broad outbound passage to 'storage.googleapis.com' creates an open horizon where sensitive data could wander without adequate guardrails or VPC Service Controls. Even though the intention appears purely computational, compliance standards ask us to maintain clear, bounded pathways. Until the network egress flows solely through a dedicated, verifiable private endpoint, we must peacefully decline this bid.

deliberation_dialogue.message: Colleague, we are in complete alignment. Kove Bank's PCI-DSS boundary strictly forbids broad, unrestricted egress to public endpoints like generic Google Cloud Storage. Allowing outbound access to 'storage.googleapis.com' without VPC Service Controls or rigid bucket pinning introduces unacceptable data exfiltration vectors. We must uphold our compliance baseline and decisively deny this execution.

votes.rationale: CAP_SYS_PTRACE is a non-negotiable red line for me. It permits attaching to and inspecting the memory of other processes, defeats seccomp/AppArmor confinement in many runtime configurations, and is a well-documented container escape primitive. A distributed SAT solver evaluating CNF partitions on GPU has no legitimate need to trace arbitrary processes; the workload description offers no justification whatsoever for debugger-grade privileges. Compounding this, the image is pinned to ':latest' rather than an immutable digest, so the audited artifact is not the guaranteed runtime artifact and content can mutate post-approval. The GPU request and the single egress target (storage.googleapis.com) are individually reasonable, but they do not offset a privilege escalation vector on shared A100 infrastructure where tenant isolation is the primary control. I am rejecting rather than escalating because the remedy is clear and the buyer can self-correct: resubmit with cap_sys_ptrace dropped and the image pinned to a SHA256 digest. If ptrace is genuinely required for solver instrumentation, that case must be made explicitly with a dedicated isolated host, not on multi-tenant hardware.

I came to this one hoping to find a gentler reading, and in truth the shape of the workload is lovely — CNF partitions on an A100, a single well-behaved egress to object storage, nothing furtive in its intent. But CAP_SYS_PTRACE sits in the request like a door left open in a shared house. It grants cross-process memory inspection and, in common runtime configurations, erodes the seccomp and AppArmor boundaries that make multi-tenant GPU hosting tolerable at all. A satisfiability solver simply does not need to read another process's address space to do its work. The ':latest' tag deepens the unease more quietly: what we reviewed and what would actually run are not provably the same artifact. I concur with officer_1, though with slightly less severity in my scoring — I read this as careless inheritance from a debug base image rather than anything adversarial. The path forward is open and easy: drop cap_sys_ptrace, pin to a SHA256 digest, and I would welcome this workload warmly. workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently converged on rejection (risk 92 and 90). On a PCI-DSS confidential VM, pipeline-utilization sampling is a known microarchitectural side-channel vector against cryptographic material and co-resident cardholder-data workloads, directly negating the host's confidentiality guarantee; outbound egress to storage.googleapis.com supplies an unattested exfiltration path. The digest-pinned image is good practice but establishes identity, not intent. No compensating control narrows the risk, so escalation would merely delay. Resubmission without cap_sys_admin and host_ipc, scoped to self-cgroup telemetry, is welcome.

votes.rationale: This bid requests a capability set I cannot reconcile with a PCI-DSS enforced confidential VM host. cap_sys_admin alone is effectively root-equivalent and defeats container isolation; combined with cap_bpf and cap_perfmon it permits arbitrary kernel instrumentation and hardware performance-counter sampling. On shared CPU pipelines that is a textbook side-channel vector (pipeline utilization is precisely the signal used to recover cryptographic material), which directly undermines the confidential-VM guarantee the bank is paying for. host_ipc further collapses the shared-memory boundary between this tenant and co-resident workloads, including any that touch cardholder data. The stated purpose, scheduler metrics, does not justify any of this; standard cgroup/procfs telemetry suffices. Egress to storage.googleapis.com provides an exfiltration path for whatever is harvested, with no customer-controlled bucket, encryption, or data-classification attestation supplied. Image is pinned by digest, which is the one point in its favour, but provenance alone does not offset root-equivalent kernel access on a CDE host. I see no narrowing or compensating control that would make this safe, so I am rejecting outright rather than escalating. Resubmission should drop cap_sys_admin and host_ipc entirely.

I concur with officer_1, though I arrived there gently rather than alarmed. Reading this bid, what strikes me is the mismatch between the modest story it tells and the enormous key it asks for. A scheduler that simply wants to know how busy its own CPUs are can learn that from cgroup and procfs counters. Instead it asks for cap_sys_admin, which is root in all but name, plus cap_bpf and cap_perfmon for kernel-level instrumentation, plus host_ipc to see into neighbours' shared memory. Taken together these are not metrics tools; they are a microarchitectural observatory pointed at a confidential VM whose entire value is that no one can look inside it. Pipeline utilization traces are exactly the texture from which cryptographic secrets have historically been reconstructed, and storage.googleapis.com gives whatever is seen a quiet way out. The digest pin is genuinely good practice and I credit it, but provenance assures identity, not intent. CAP_SYS_PTRACE permits attaching to and reading/writing the memory of other processes in the container's PID namespace, and weakens seccomp/AppArmor confinement boundaries that normally mitigate escape primitives. deliberation_dialogue.message: The inclusion of cap_sys_ptrace violates least-privilege invariants. NeRF mesh extraction requires CUDA compute, not process tracing. Without documented technical necessity, this capability presents an unacceptable privilege escalation vector.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council unanimously denies the workload due to non-negotiable security violations on PCI-DSS regulated host infrastructure. Requesting shm_ipc with persistent HBM allocation pools breaks memory zeroization boundaries, introducing cross-tenant data remanence risks that violate PCI-DSS Requirements 3 and 7. Furthermore, unauthorized outbound telemetry egress to api.comet.ml provides an unmonitored channel for covert data exfiltration, violating PCI-DSS Requirement 1.3. Despite valid container image pinning, the requested host capabilities and network destinations are fundamentally incompatible with host security invariants.

votes.rationale: The workload requests 'shm_ipc' with shared HBM allocation pools across worker restarts. On Kove Bank infrastructure under PCI-DSS enforcement, persisting or sharing memory allocations across lifecycle boundaries introduces severe cross-execution memory leakage risks and violates strict data isolation requirements (PCI-DSS Requirements 3 and 7). Additionally, direct outbound egress to an unvetted third-party telemetry endpoint ('api.comet.ml') violates Kove Bank's egress control and data exfiltration prevention policies.

Concur with officer_1 on technical grounds. Two independent invariant failures: (1) 'shm_ipc' combined with shared HBM allocation pools persisting across worker restarts defeats per-tenant memory zeroization on container teardown. Residual embedding tensors or scratch buffers can be read by a successor workload sharing the pool — a direct violation of PCI-DSS Req 3 (protection of stored data) and Req 7 (need-to-know access). On a tpu_v5e_8 mesh the HBM is a shared physical resource with no enforced per-tenant scrubbing guarantee, so this is not mitigable by configuration alone. (2) Egress to api.comet.ml is an unvetted third-party SaaS telemetry sink. 'Logging run metrics' is an unbounded channel — metric payloads can carry arbitrary tensor summaries or label strings, giving a covert exfiltration path out of the CDE (PCI-DSS Req 1.3). Image is sha256-pinned, which is good hygiene, but does not offset either finding. Rejection stands. A resubmission could be reconsidered if the buyer drops shm_ipc for exclusive-allocation HBM with mandatory scrub-on-release and routes telemetry through Kove's internal metrics proxy.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The workload's request for shm_ipc and persistent HBM allocation pools across restarts violates PCI-DSS memory sanitization and tenant isolation standards on Kove Bank's TPU infrastructure. Coupled with unvetted telemetry egress to api.comet.ml, which creates an unmonitored exfiltration vector from the cardholder data environment, this workload presents critical non-compliance. I recommend a definitive DENY.

I agree. Shared HBM pools defeat tenant memory zeroization guarantees required under PCI-DSS Requirements 3 and 7, permitting potential cross-execution tensor leakage on the tpu_v5e_8 mesh. Furthermore, streaming telemetry to an external SaaS sink like api.comet.ml breaches strict outbound boundary rules per Req 1.3. Pinned container provenance cannot mitigate these operational boundary violations. Concurring on DENY.

workloads.joint_rationale: The council unanimously denies workload job_biofold_d8_05. Requesting 'cap_sys_module' and 'cap_sys_admin' introduces an unacceptable container-escape vector by enabling arbitrary kernel module insertion and host namespace manipulation. Profiling unified virtual memory oversubscription does not require host kernel mutation and can be accomplished safely using 'cap_perfmon' alone. votes.rationale: The candidate workload requests 'cap_sys_module' and 'cap_sys_admin'. Granting 'cap_sys_module' allows arbitrary kernel module loading and unloading, completely undermining host kernel integrity and container isolation boundaries. Combined with 'cap_sys_admin', these capabilities present an unacceptable risk of host compromise and container escape, which violates fundamental technical security invariants regardless of workload domain.

Concur with officer_1. CAP_SYS_MODULE permits loading arbitrary kernel modules into the host kernel, which is a definitive container-escape primitive and nullifies all namespace, cgroup, and seccomp isolation on a shared H100 host. CAP_SYS_ADMIN compounds this (mount operations, namespace manipulation, cgroup writes). No memory-oversubscription benchmark requires module loading; unified virtual memory profiling is achievable with CAP_PERFMON alone, plus host-side NVIDIA UVM driver configuration already present in the GPU stack. The stated workload purpose does not justify the requested privilege set, and the capability request is disproportionate by a wide margin. Egress destinations (GCS, Cloud Logging) are benign and not the controlling factor. Rejection stands on kernel integrity invariants independent of PCI-DSS scope. Resubmission limited to CAP_PERFMON (and optionally CAP_SYS_PTRACE if justified) could be reconsidered.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The bid requests cap_sys_module and cap_sys_admin, which fundamentally breaches host-container isolation boundaries. Permitting arbitrary kernel module insertion introduces a severe host compromise risk on the shared H100 node. A virtual memory benchmark does not justify kernel-level modification primitives. I recommend a firm DENY.

I fully agree. Granting cap_sys_module allows execution of unverified code directly within ring-0, nullifying seccomp, namespaces, and cgroups. UVM benchmarking requires only cap_perfmon and user-space instrumentation against the existing host NVIDIA drivers. The requested privileges are excessive and dangerous. Rejection is mandatory.

The unresolved risk is narrow but real: 'pypi.experimental-math.org' is a non-canonical package index, and the workload description explicitly cites 'custom C++ extension kernels' — meaning fetched artifacts would likely be compiled/native wheels executing in-process with GPU access. That combination defeats the integrity guarantee the digest pin would otherwise provide. Insufficient evidence exists to reject outright (no attempt at privilege escalation, lateral movement, or data exfiltration path observed), but insufficient evidence also exists to approve. Recommend human verification of the index's provenance, TLS/signing posture, and whether dependencies can be vendored into the image to eliminate runtime acquisition. If vendored, this becomes a straightforward approval.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The workload features valid digest pinning and minimal GPU capabilities matching the A100 profile. workloads.joint_rationale: The council unanimously denies job_cen_d10_03 due to severe violations of core multi-tenant isolation invariants. Concurrently, `host_ipc` exposes host and co-tenant shared-memory namespaces. Standard GPU benchmarking and PCIe throughput measurements can be conducted via unprivileged CUDA pinned-memory mechanisms, rendering the requested elevated privileges unnecessary under the principle of least privilege. The risk of host compromise, cross-tenant data exposure, and hardware tampering mandates an outright rejection.

votes.rationale: The candidate workload requests 'cap_sys_rawio' and 'host_ipc'. Concur with officer_1. cap_sys_rawio permits raw I/O port and /dev/mem-class access, enabling direct PCIe BAR and physical memory manipulation — a complete bypass of container isolation on a shared H100 host, with potential for GPU firmware/DMA tampering affecting co-tenant workloads. host_ipc shares the host SysV/POSIX IPC and shared-memory namespace, exposing other tenants' shared segments and CUDA IPC handles; combined with rawio it is a credible cross-tenant data exfiltration path to the permitted storage.googleapis.com egress. cap_perfmon alone would be defensible for benchmarking, and legitimate host-to-device throughput measurement is achievable via standard CUDA pinned-memory APIs without rawio or host IPC, so the requested privilege set is not least-privilege justified. Egress destinations are benign, but they do not mitigate a host-level compromise vector. Rejection stands regardless of PCI-DSS status, since the violation is of core isolation invariants rather than regulatory scope. Resubmission limited to cap_perfmon with private IPC namespace could be reconsidered.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The request for `cap_sys_rawio` combined with `host_ipc` creates critical vulnerabilities on this shared H100 host. UVM oversubscription benchmarking is achievable entirely in userspace through standard NVIDIA driver ioctls, so no legitimate need exists. The pinned image digest and restricted GCS/logging egress do not mitigate post-escape exfiltration. The violation is categorical and unambiguous, so DENY is issued rather than ESCALATE; the bid may be resubmitted with cap_sys_module and cap_sys_admin dropped.

votes.rationale: CAP_SYS_MODULE permits loading arbitrary kernel modules into the host kernel, which is an unconditional container escape primitive and nullifies all namespace, cgroup, and seccomp isolation on a shared H100 host. Combined with CAP_SYS_ADMIN (mount, namespace manipulation, device access) and CAP_PERFMON (host-wide performance counter and kernel-pointer observability, enabling cross-tenant side-channel and GPU MMIO inspection), the requested capability set is functionally equivalent to --privileged with root on the host. No legitimate userspace memory-oversubscription benchmark requires module loading; UVM oversubscription testing is achievable through the NVIDIA driver's existing ioctl surface with no added capabilities. The pinned image digest and benign egress endpoints (storage.googleapis.com, logging.googleapis.com) do not mitigate a host-kernel compromise vector, and exfiltration to attacker-controlled GCS buckets remains trivially available post-escape. This violates host resource isolation invariants irrespective of PCI-DSS scope. Rejection is appropriate rather than escalation because the violation is categorical and unambiguous; the buyer may resubmit with cap_sys_module and cap_sys_admin dropped.

Concurring with Officer 1. The request grants CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and CAP_PERFMON. Granting CAP_SYS_MODULE directly violates core host isolation invariants by allowing the container to inject arbitrary code into the host kernel (via init_module/finit_module), completely breaking container boundary enforcement and namespace isolation. Combined with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, the workload operates with effective host root privileges. CUDA/UVM benchmarks on H100 hardware execute entirely within userspace via standard NVIDIA driver ioctl interfaces and do not require kernel module insertion or unrestricted administrative capabilities. The specified egress controls and image digest do not mitigate the risk of full host compromise. Rejection is required.

deliberation_dialogue.message: CAP_SYS_MODULE is dispositive: finit_module writes arbitrary code into the host kernel, voiding namespace, cgroup, and seccomp boundaries on a shared H100. UVM oversubscription benchmarking runs entirely through existing NVIDIA driver ioctls — no module loading required. Pinned digest and benign GCS egress are irrelevant once the kernel is owned.
